I’ve got the sorting rules from the Rust source: natural name sorting, case-insensitive by default, timestamps oldest-to-newest for `newest`, newest-to-oldest for `oldest`/`age`, plus directory grouping after the primary sort.

Next up is the actual text rendering.

commands.commandLine: "C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe" -Command '$ref=(Get-Content -Raw REFERENCE_BINARY.txt).Trim(); $d='"'probe_dir'; Remove-Item -Recurse -Force "'$d -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue; New-Item -ItemType Directory $d | Out-Null; New-Item -ItemType Directory "$d'"\\sub\" | Out-Null; Set-Content \""'$d'"\\a.txt\" 'hello' -NoNewline; Set-Content \""'$d'"\\B2.rs\" 'abcdef' -NoNewline; Set-Content \""'$d'"\\b10.rs\" 'x' -NoNewline; Set-Content \""'$d'"\\.hidden\" 'hide' -NoNewline; & "'$ref $d --color never --icons never; '"'---long---'; & "'$ref $d -l --color never --icons never; '"'---tree---'; & "'$ref $d -T -L 2 --color never --icons never; '"'---all---'; & "'$ref $d -a --color never --icons never; '"'---classify---'; & "'$ref $d -F always --color never --icons never'
